title: Granular capture rollback and KV reconcile for non-blocking prefill/decode schedules
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: The runtime occasionally observes nonblocking prefill/decode schedules where partial CUDA graph captures succeed across a subset of streams, but subsequent replays diverge due to KV cache state differences and out-of-order kernel binding. This ticket designs and implements a fine-grained capture rollback and KV reconcile mechanism that: 1) isolates minimal capture segments that can be atomically rolled back on conflict, 2) computes a minimal reconcile plan to merge KV cache deltas deterministically, and 3) integrates lightweight conflict detection to avoid coarse-grained full-graph fallbacks. The goal is to reduce the rate of conservative full-graph recaptures and fallback replays while preserving deterministic outputs and token atomicity.
technical_design: Design highlights: - Capture segmentation: break long prefill sequences into idempotent micro-capture segments (segment boundary rules based on token horizon, attention pattern changes, and kernel affinity). - Rollback protocol: on detection of cross-stream capture inconsistency, use segment-level fencing to rollback only the affected segments rather than entire graph. Rollback includes restoring stream-local allocator/descriptor state and invalidating per-segment kernel bindings. - KV reconcile algorithm: maintain per-segment KV delta logs (append-only small deltas). On replay divergence, compare segment deltas using hash-and-snapshot tokens; if deltas are commutative, merge; otherwise apply deterministic last-writer-wins based on capture epoch plus tie-breaker by stream priority. - Conflict detection: lightweight checksum of attention key/value tensors per segment using 64-bit xxHash to detect divergence with low overhead. - Scheduling hooks: extend the scheduler to tag requests with capture epochs and segment ids; routing will prefer replay-compatible streams. - Fallback curve: if repeated rollbacks exceed threshold for an epoch, escalate to conservative recapture for that model/length to avoid repeated churn. Implementation notes: leverage existing graph-capture APIs but add SegmentCapture object, KVDelta log storage in pinned GPU memory, and reconcile path in C++ runtime with CUDA streams synchronization primitives. Unit-tested low-level primitives and end-to-end fuzz harness for multi-stream interleavings.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reduction in full-graph recapture rate by at least 40% on mixed short/long request workloads in lab benchmark compared to baseline.
2) No observed correctness regressions on deterministic replay test harness (100k synthetic sessions).
3) Latency impact <2% p99 added overhead for capture bookkeeping on standard throughput workloads.
4) Rollout plan and canary with autoscaling and metrics defined in rollout section.

T3: Integrate reconcile path and deterministic merge strategy (Marco + Yuki)
T4: Add scheduler tagging and epoch propagation (Selene)

tests: Unit tests for SegmentCapture rollback and state restore (GPU-local)
Deterministic replay harness with seeded RNG and 100k session sweep
Fuzzing across stream interleavings with mutated KV deltas
Bench: mixed QPS workload with 32/128/512 token distributions to measure recapture rate and latency overhead
Canary: 1% traffic on runtime-1.20 with golden outputs compared to baseline for 48h
rollout: Phased canary: - Canary 1 (1%): runtime-1.20 on non-critical region for 48 hours, continuous correctness verification against golden harness. - Canary 2 (10%): 72 hours with autoscaling stress and SLO monitors. - Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over one week depending on metrics. Monitors: recapture-rate, rollback-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, token-atomicity-checkfailures, KV-reconcile-merge-rate. Rollback threshold defaults (3 attempts) configurable via runtime flag for canary tuning.
risks: Reconcile tie-breaker may hide subtle semantic differences for rare attention layouts — risk of silent correctness if merging is not conservative enough.
Overhead of per-segment checksums could increase tail latency for small-request workloads if not optimized.
Edge cases with mixed-quant kernels where KV tensor representation differs across streams; reconcile needs representation normalization.
Increased complexity in scheduler tagging could interact with existing autoscaler heuristics causing delayed scale-up decisions.
open_questions: Q1: Should tie-breaker policy prefer host-prioritized streams or lowest-latency stream? (ops vs correctness trade-off)
Q2: Which hashing primitive gives best speed-vs-collision trade-off on GPU memory snapshots? (xxHash64 chosen for prototype)
Q3: Retention window for KVDelta logs per segment — bytes and eviction policy?
Q4: How to expose reconcile diagnostics in the Console without leaking model internals?
